limitations: Silent MCD/STOI scored against the method's own vocoded pseudo targets; 18 of 81 speakers excluded by the method's DTW cost; the w/o DAT ablation also removes vocalized training; single runs, no seeds; prior DTW target transfer in EMG uncited.

title: WESPER: Zero-shot and Realtime Whisper to Normal Voice Conversion for Whisper-based Speech Interactions
venue: Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '23)
authors: Jun Rekimoto
summary: WESPER trains a whisper-to-normal converter with no paired data (M02, ahead); its unit route (M06) is untested against baselines, and its ASR gain trails a recognizer fine-tuned on labelled whisper.
sensor: Ordinary microphone (whispered speech)
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: WER 44.70 to 26.68 (CER 28.38 to 12.70) on wTIMIT whispers, Google ASR
limitations: Relies on whispered rather than truly silent speech and is evaluated on whisper datasets, not silent-speech benchmarks or broad public use.

title: Zero-Shot Personalized Lip-to-Speech Synthesis with Face Image Based Voice Control
authors: Zheng-Yan Sheng; Yang Ai; Zhen-Hua Ling
summary: Face-image voice control (M07) and VAE/cross-modal training (M03) are standard: Facetron did face-derived zero-shot voice on GRID in 2021; face EER 36.72 vs 26.57 with reference audio; no WER.
sensor: Camera (lip video plus face image)
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: Unseen GRID speakers (13): face-image control EER 36.72 vs 26.57 with reference speech, MOS-FVM 3.133 vs 3.172; ESTOI 0.389; no ASR word error reported.
limitations: Face-derived zero-shot voice predates it (Facetron 2021); no WER; Table 2 scores the reference-speech variant; Griffin-Lim waveform; GRID only, no seeds; overlap of GRID with pretraining identities not stated.

title: EarCommand: "Hearing" Your Silent Speech Commands In Ear
authors: Yincheng Jin; Yang Gao; Xuhai Xu; Seokmin Choi; Jiyang Li; Feng Liu; Zhengxiong Li; Zhanpeng Jin
summary: Earphone SSI senses ear-canal deformation with inaudible in-ear echoes to recognize silently mouthed commands; abstract reports 10.02% WER on 32 word commands and 12.33% on 25 sentence commands.
sensor: Earbud with inward-facing speaker and microphone (near-ultrasound echoes in ear canal)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: WER 10.02% (word commands), 12.33% (sentence commands)
limitations: Reviewed from abstract and press only; closed command sets; participant count and calibration details unverified.

title: FastLTS: Non-Autoregressive End-to-End Unconstrained Lip-to-Speech Synthesis
authors: Yongqi Wang; Zhou Zhao
summary: FastLTS is a non-autoregressive end-to-end lip-to-speech system that makes unconstrained synthesis substantially faster without obvious quality loss, evaluated on Lip2Wav and GRID.
sensor: Silent talking-face video
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Benchmark corpora only with three speakers per dataset slice; no in-the-wild user study or live camera-to-audio latency test.

title: Improved Processing of Ultrasound Tongue Videos by Combining ConvLSTM and 3D Convolutional Networks
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth
summary: Combines 3D CNNs and ConvLSTM to regress mel-spectrograms from ultrasound tongue video, modestly outperforming prior architectures in accuracy and efficiency on single-speaker Hungarian data.
sensor: Micro ultrasound tongue probe with headset, plus microphone
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: MSE ~0.276, mean R2 ~0.73 on mel-spectrogram regression
limitations: Single-speaker dataset with no perceptual intelligibility testing, cross-speaker evaluation, or real-time tests.

title: Learning Audio-Visual Speech Representation by Masked Multimodal Cluster Prediction
authors: Bowen Shi; Wei-Ning Hsu; Kushal Lakhotia; Abdelrahman Mohamed
summary: AV-HuBERT's masked audio-visual cluster pre-training (M03) was a large step past distillation, but its LRS3 gains lack repeated runs and later work beats it at matched budgets.
sensor: Camera and microphone (audio-visual video; video-only at lipreading inference)
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: 32.5% WER (30 h labels), 26.9% WER (433 h + self-training) on LRS3 lipreading
limitations: Vocalized English TED-style video only; no silent-articulation, real-time or on-device evaluation; heavy pretraining compute.

title: Lip-to-Speech Synthesis for Arbitrary Speakers in the Wild
venue: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM '22)
authors: Sindhu B Hegde; K R Prajwal; Rudrabha Mukhopadhyay; Vinay P Namboodiri; C. V. Jawahar
summary: VAE-GAN lip-to-speech with a reference-audio voice: a standard design whose gains are in distribution and sync metrics; no WER is reported, behind its own lineage on evaluation.
sensor: Silent lip/face video plus a one-second reference-audio clip for the voice
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: LRS2 FDSD 1.273 (lip-to-text plus TTS 0.984) and LSE-C 2.507; PESQ/STOI 0.60/0.34, below the sequence-to-sequence baseline (0.97/0.43); no WER reported
limitations: No word error rate on the output; listener test on 15 LRS2 samples; voice reference source at test not stated; SED not shown to be independent of the voice-loss identity network; single runs; struggles with non-frontal faces and produces wrong words.

title: Movement Detection of Tongue and Related Body Parts Using IR-UWB Radar
authors: Sunghwa Lee; Younghoon Shin
summary: Uses IR-UWB radar aimed at the chin to detect hidden tongue movement states, achieving at least 90% accuracy for each of four participants on a binary task.
sensor: IR-UWB radar with sinuous antennas and dielectric lens
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: >=90% accuracy per participant, 2 tongue states, 4 participants
limitations: Only two states, four participants, manual trial boundaries, stationary lab setup; no continuous speech, unseen-user, or vocabulary-level tests.

title: Sequence-to-Sequence Voice Reconstruction for Silent Speech in a Tonal Language
authors: Huiyan Li; Haohong Lin; You Wang; Hengyang Wang; Ming Zhang; Han Gao; Qing Ai; Zhiyuan Luo; Guang Li
summary: Duration-regulated seq2seq with toneme loss voices silent Mandarin EMG; gains rest on the auxiliary loss, not the architecture, and prompt grouping in the utterance split is unreported.
sensor: Five facial wet Ag/AgCl sEMG channels, 2000 Hz
speaker: Speaker-dependent (six speakers, one model each)
key_result: 21.99% objective ASR CER (MASR, mean of six speakers), stated as 24.63% better than the Gaddy-Klein 2020 baseline (absolute or relative not stated); 6.41% listener CER; single runs, utterance-level split with five repetitions per prompt and no stated prompt grouping
limitations: Gain confounded by an auxiliary toneme loss the baseline lacks; length regulator never ablated and the model fails without the toneme loss; tone changes CER by +6.51 in one run; units of Table VI changes unstated; prompt grouping in the split not reported; no seeds, significance test or latency; MASR checkpoint unstated.

title: SilentSpeller: Towards mobile, hands-free, silent speech text entry using electropalatography
authors: Naoki Kimura; Tan Gemicioglu; Jonathan Womack; Yuhui Zhao; Richard Li; Abdelkareem Bedri; Zixiong Su; Alex Olwal; Jun Rekimoto; Thad Starner
summary: SilentSpeller enables silent spelling text entry with an in-mouth electropalatography retainer, reaching 37 wpm at 87% accuracy in live entry and comparable accuracy while walking.
sensor: SmartPalate retainer, 124 capacitive electrodes (EPG)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Live entry 37 wpm at 87% accuracy (best 53 wpm, 91%); 92% word accuracy offline
limitations: Strongly user-dependent; requires an obtrusive custom-fitted in-mouth retainer; offline tuning used only two main participants.

title: Sub-word Level Lip Reading With Visual Attention
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
authors: K. R. Prajwal; Triantafyllos Afouras; Andrew Zisserman
summary: Attention pooling of the lip map (M06) was ahead in 2021 but not the route to later SOTA; WordPiece output (M08) was preceded by BPE in 2020; the SOTA table mixes data budgets.
sensor: Camera (face/lip video of voiced speech, audio unused)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 22.6% WER on LRS2, 30.7% on LRS3 (extended training); 28.9%/40.6% public data only
limitations: Camera-only lip reading rather than articulatory SSI; offline benchmark results only, with no live silent dictation, latency, privacy or in-the-wild evaluation.

title: SVTS: Scalable Video-to-Speech Synthesis
authors: Rodrigo Mira; Alexandros Haliassos; Stavros Petridis; Björn W. Schuller; Maja Pantic
summary: SVTS shows a simple spectrogram predictor with a pretrained vocoder outperforms prior complex video-to-speech models and scales to large datasets such as LRS3+VoxCeleb2.
sensor: Camera (lip video)
speaker: Both
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Depends on large curated aligned datasets; weaker on unseen speakers and unconstrained conditions; no LRS3 WER or user study.

title: Towards Neural Decoding of Imagined Speech based on Spoken Speech
authors: Seo-Hyun Lee; Young-Eun Lee; Soowon Kim; Byung-Kwan Ko; Seong-Whan Lee
summary: Transfers CSP+SVM models trained on spoken-speech EEG to imagined speech decoding; accuracy is slightly lower but not significantly different from direct training in a 5-class, 7-subject offline task.
sensor: 64-channel active-electrode EEG cap (10-10 system)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 26.8% accuracy (transfer) vs 30.5% direct, 5 classes, 7 subjects, p=0.098
limitations: Small offline within-subject study with only 5 classes and 7 subjects; no online, cross-subject, or larger-vocabulary evaluation.

title: VCVTS: Multi-speaker Video-to-Speech synthesis via cross-modal knowledge transfer from voice conversion
authors: Disong Wang; Shan Yang; Dan Su; Xunying Liu; Dong Yu; Helen Meng
summary: VCVTS performs multi-speaker video-to-speech synthesis by transferring knowledge from voice conversion, with speaker control from reference speech, on GRID and LRW.
sensor: Silent lip video plus reference speech
speaker: Both
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Large seen/unseen speaker gap and vocoder-dependent quality; offline benchmarks only, requires reference speech, not validated interactively.

title: VisageSynTalk: Unseen Speaker Video-to-Speech Synthesis via Speech-Visage Feature Selection
authors: Joanna Hong; Minsu Kim; Yong Man Ro
summary: VisageSynTalk disentangles speech content and visage (identity) features for video-to-speech synthesis, yielding robust results for unseen speakers on benchmarks.
sensor: Talking-face video
speaker: Both
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Offline benchmarks only with a small MOS study (20 GRID samples, 16 raters); needs clean aligned video, no robustness to pose or occlusion.

title: Visual Speech Recognition for Multiple Languages in the Wild
authors: Pingchuan Ma; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: Joint distillation losses are a standard idea worth 1.5-2.0 LRS3 points, less than recipe and masking; LRS3 31.5% trails 16.9% from public data; 4 of 6 languages lack external baselines.
sensor: Camera (face/lip video)
vocabulary: Open vocabulary; English, Mandarin, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, French
speaker: Speaker-independent
key_result: 25.5% WER LRS2, 31.5% WER LRS3, 8.0% CER CMLR (best of ten runs)
limitations: Vocalized in-the-wild video only; silent speech untested; small non-English test sets and offline evaluation.

title: VisualTTS: TTS with Accurate Lip-Speech Synchronization for Automatic Voice Over
authors: Junchen Lu; Berrak Sisman; Rui Liu; Mingyang Zhang; Haizhou Li
summary: VisualTTS conditions TTS on silent lip video to improve lip-speech synchronization for automatic voice-over, evaluated on the scripted GRID corpus.
sensor: Mono video camera (lip region) plus text script
speaker: Not stated
key_result: LSE-C 5.87, LSE-D 8.45, MOS 4.17 on GRID test set
limitations: Restricted to scripted GRID data with paired text; no unseen speakers, spontaneous speech, or real-time tests; does not decode silent speech.

title: Advances and Challenges in Deep Lip Reading
authors: Marzieh Oghbaie; Arian Sabaghi; Kooshan Hashemifard; Mohammad Akbari
summary: Survey of deep lip reading covering datasets, pipeline modules, challenges and evaluation metrics; contributes no new model or experiments.
sensor: Video (lip/face)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Literature synthesis only, with no original experiments or deployment evaluation.

title: An Improved Model for Voicing Silent Speech
venue: Proceedings of the 59th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics and the 11th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing (Volume 2: Short Papers)
authors: David Gaddy; Dan Klein
summary: Conv-plus-Transformer EMG encoder (M06) is reused by the 2026 state of the art; the phoneme loss (M02) follows 2018 ultrasound work. Single runs; ablations explain 16.3 of 25.8 points.
sensor: Facial surface EMG electrodes
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 42.2% automatic WER (DeepSpeech) from 68.0%, single runs; 32.3% mean human WER from two listeners on 40 samples; a later rerun of the model scores 25.74% under Whisper; one speaker, open vocabulary
limitations: One speaker; no seeds or reruns; ablations account for 16.3 of the 25.8-point gain only if effects add, while alignment and batching changes are not ablated; DeepSpeech version and scorer unstated; test split inherited from 2020 with no held-out session; last-epoch checkpoint; human check of 40 samples by two listeners 7.6 points apart.

title: Convolutional Neural Network-Based Age Estimation Using B-Mode Ultrasound Tongue Image
authors: Kele Xu; Tamas Gabor Csapo; Ming Feng
summary: Exploratory CNN regression of child age from tongue ultrasound images, reaching validation MSE 2.03 on UXTD versus 3.64 for a mean-age baseline.
sensor: B-mode ultrasound tongue images
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Validation MSE 2.03 on UXTD (baseline 3.64); 4.87 on UPX (baseline 5.35)
limitations: Not an SSI system; small child-only datasets, validation-set error only, and no external dataset or deployment test.

title: EMA2S: An End-to-End Multimodal Articulatory-to-Speech System
venue: 2021 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
authors: Yu-Wen Chen; Kuo-Hsuan Hung; Shang-Yi Chuang; Jonathan Sherman; Wen-Chin Huang; Xugang Lu; Yu Tsao
summary: Speech-latent target (M02) has a 2017 precedent and small, mixed single-run gains; spectrogram-loss-only end-to-end loses to WORLD (M06); a preference test replaces listener transcription (M12).
sensor: EMA with nine sensors (lips, jaw, tongue)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Small dataset (three speakers, 354 utterances each), small listening test, no cross-speaker testing, and intrusive lab-grade EMA hardware.

title: End-to-End Silent Speech Recognition with Acoustic Sensing
authors: Jian Luo; Jianzong Wang; Ning Cheng; Guilin Jiang; Jing Xiao
summary: Standard on sensing and decoding: phone-sonar phase features and an attention decoder work on 54 mouthed sentences of 29 words; the cross-user claim rests on tuning data that include the test users.
sensor: Smartphone speaker and microphone, 8 near-ultrasonic carriers (17–23 kHz), I/Q phase features
task: Silent sentence recognition from lip movements (active acoustic sensing)
vocabulary: 54 fixed Standard Chinese sentences built from 29 words
speaker: 10 volunteers; random split, leave-one-domain-out (user and position) and leave-one-sentence-out tests
session: 5 sessions per volunteer on different days; split across sessions not stated
key_result: WER 2.6% (random split), 8.4% (leave-one-domain-out), 8.1% (leave-one-sentence-out); attention beats CTC by 0.7 to 2.1 points.
limitations: Closed 29-word vocabulary; hyperparameters tuned on a random split that includes held-out users; one run per test, no seeds; phase gain shown in one ablation; no latency or power figures.

title: Improving Neural Silent Speech Interface Models by Adversarial Training
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth; Gábor Gosztolya; Alexandra Markó; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Standard on the adversarial loss (M02): it predates the paper in video-to-speech and its gains are small, with no variance reported; behind on evaluation (M12): no listening test.
sensor: Midsagittal ultrasound tongue imaging, Articulate Instruments Micro, 82 fps, resized to 64x128
task: Ultrasound-to-mel-spectrogram mapping with a 3D CNN, WaveGlow synthesis; MSE-only versus MSE plus Patch-GAN adversarial loss
vocabulary: Read sentences (Hungarian; English TaL1), vocalized; vocabulary not stated
speaker: One speaker per corpus (Hungarian female; TaL1 English); train and test from the same speaker
session: Not stated; split procedure not given (counts only), no held-out session reported
key_result: Test STOI 0.7050 to 0.7067 (Hungarian) and 0.612 to 0.623 (English); MCD 4.627 to 4.558 and 3.38 to 3.229 dB; no variance reported, no listening test.
limitations: No repeated runs or variance reported; MSE-only baseline also loses on MSE; output window changed for the GAN runs; loss weights selected on an unstated set; objective metrics only, including SDR and SI-SDR on vocoded speech; one speaker per corpus.

title: Multi-modality Associative Bridging through Memory: Speech Sound Recollected from Face Video
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
authors: Minsu Kim; Joanna Hong; Se Jin Park; Yong Man Ro
summary: Audio memory recall (M02) is ahead as a design, but the LRW state-of-the-art claim misses a prior 87.9% model, the edge over distillation is one run, and GRID gains are small.
sensor: Silent face video
task: Lip reading and speech synthesis from video
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: LRW 85.41% (+1.27 over baseline, +0.91 over distillation), below a prior 87.9% single model; LRW-1000 50.82% (+5.89), 2.8 above the best prior model without word boundaries; GRID seen speakers STOI 0.738 vs 0.731 (Lip2Wav), no WER
limitations: Best memory size of an ablation, one run, with no stated validation rule; edge over distillation is one LRW run; LRW state-of-the-art claim misses a prior 87.9% model and the LRW-1000 lead holds only without word boundaries; no GRID no-memory score in the main text; GRID objective scores use Griffin-Lim and the MOS gain comes from WaveNet; no WER; offline only.

title: Neural Speaker Embeddings for Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; László Tóth; Gábor Gosztolya; Alexandra Markó; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Standard on embedding conditioning (2.4% relative MSE gain on seen speakers); behind on speaker recognition, which never separates speaker from recording session.
sensor: Midsagittal ultrasound tongue imaging, Articulate Instruments Micro, 82 fps (TaL80 corpus)
task: Speaker recognition from ultrasound (x-vector) and multi-speaker ultrasound-to-mel-spectrum estimation conditioned on it
speaker: x-vector trained on 50 speakers, scored on 31 held-out speakers; SSI trained and tested on the same 31 speakers
session: About one TaL80 recording session per speaker (inferred from corpus totals); speaker and session not separated
key_result: 0.70% 1-NN speaker error on 31 held-out speakers (pooled segments); x-vector input lowers multi-speaker test MSE from 0.669 to 0.653, 2.4% relative, one reported run.
limitations: Speaker recognition not tested across sessions; SSI tested only on seen speakers; single runs without seeds or chance levels; no listening, MCD or intelligibility score for multi-speaker systems.

title: Neuroprosthesis for decoding speech in a paralyzed person with anarthria
authors: David A. Moses; Sean L. Metzger; Jessie R. Liu; Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Joseph G. Makin; Pengfei F. Sun; Josh Chartier; Maximilian E. Dougherty; Patricia M. Liu; Gary M. Abrams; Adelyn Tu-Chan; Karunesh Ganguly; Edward F. Chang
summary: Sentence decoding from a person who cannot speak holds for 50 words and one participant; the decoder is standard, and an LM restricted to the test vocabulary drives the gain.
sensor: 128-electrode high-density ECoG over sensorimotor cortex
task: Attempted word and sentence decoding to text
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Median WER 25.6% with LM (60.5% without), 15.2 wpm; isolated words 47.1% (chance 2%)
limitations: Single participant, 50-word vocabulary, strong reliance on the language model, spurious detections, no independent use.

title: Silent Speech and Emotion Recognition from Vocal Tract Shape Dynamics in Real-Time MRI
authors: Laxmi Pandey; Ahmed Sabbir Arif
summary: Sentence-level speech recognition from real-time MRI of the vocal tract, plus emotion and gender articulation analysis; reaches 40.6% PER on USC-TIMIT with a language model, beating earlier rtMRI baselines.
sensor: Real-time MRI scanner (full vocal tract)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 40.6% PER on USC-TIMIT unseen data with language model
limitations: rtMRI is a large, immobile lab instrument with no deployable path; evidence limited to offline decoding on USC-TIMIT.

title: Silent versus modal multi-speaker speech recognition from ultrasound and video
authors: Manuel Sam Ribeiro; Aciel Eshky; Korin Richmond; Steve Renals
summary: Standard on both changed components: modal-to-silent loss and fMLLR were known; later work narrows the absolute gap but not the fMLLR ratio, and adaptation gains rest on single runs.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging and lip video (TaL corpus)
task: Sentence recognition from articulatory images: modal-trained, tested on modal, silent and whispered speech
vocabulary: Read TaL prompts; in-domain bigram LM on a superset of the corpus prompts
speaker: Multi-speaker (82 speakers, test speakers seen in training) and speaker-dependent (TaL1)
session: TaL1: per-session fMLLR; test sessions not stated
key_result: Modal-trained recognition: TaL80 silent WER 70.21 vs modal 39.79 with fMLLR (30.42 points, about 76% higher); unsupervised adaptation adds at most 3.36 silent points and raises modal WER; a later system on TaL narrows the absolute gap to 20.28 points but keeps the fMLLR ratio near 1.75.
limitations: Test speakers are in the training set; single runs with no seeds or significance tests; adaptation is scored on its own adaptation data; LM test-prompt inclusion not stated; correlations of WER with duration and tongue space have no intervals.

title: Speaker disentanglement in video-to-speech conversion
authors: Dan Oneață; Adriana Stan; Horia Cucu
summary: Speaker-conditioned video-to-speech with adversarial identity removal: both standard (gradient reversal on GRID lips dates from 2017); EER uses the training embedding network; one run.
sensor: Camera (silent lip video) plus speaker embedding
speaker: Both
key_result: About 38.9% WER, 11.9% EER (gradient reversal), unseen speaker identity control, GRID
limitations: Closed-vocabulary read GRID speech only; intelligibility-control trade-off worsens on unseen speakers and speaker identity or embedding is required at inference.

title: Speech Synthesis from Text and Ultrasound Tongue Image-based Articulatory Input
authors: Tamas Gabor Csapo; Laszlo Toth; Gabor Gosztolya; Alexandra Marko
summary: Limited-data TTS augmented with ultrasound tongue images; combined text plus ultrasound gives the lowest test MCD for all 8 speakers, while ultrasound-only input remains far worse.
sensor: Micro ultrasound system with probe-fixing headset
task: Speech synthesis from text plus ultrasound
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Test MCD 5.442 (text+ultrasound) vs 5.652 (text-only) vs 7.153 (ultrasound-only), speaker 03mn
limitations: Not a standalone SSI: best system still needs text input; speaker-dependent, limited data, sensitive to probe misalignment, and no listening tests.

title: Voice Activity Detection for Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interfaces using Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Amin Honarmandi Shandiz; Laszlo Toth
summary: CNN speech-versus-silence detection from ultrasound tongue images on one speaker (TaL1), reaching 85.2% test accuracy; removing silence slightly improves downstream SSI reconstruction (MCD 3.05 vs 3.12).
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 85.2% test accuracy, F1 0.9, ROC AUC 0.859, single speaker
limitations: Single-speaker data with speech-derived labels; no cross-speaker validation, live test, or robustness to probe shift and new users.

title: 3D Convolutional Neural Networks for Ultrasound-Based Silent Speech Interfaces
venue: Artificial Intelligence and Soft Computing (ICAISC 2020), Lecture Notes in Computer Science 12415
authors: László Tóth; Amin Honarmandi Shandiz
summary: (2+1)D front end (M06) is standard: established in lip reading, ported to ultrasound; a 6.3% MSE edge over CNN+LSTM, one speaker, one run; MSE-only evaluation (M12 behind).
sensor: Micro ultrasound system, 64-element convex transducer, 82 fps
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Test MSE of 13 standardized vocoder parameters: 3D (2+1)D CNN 0.315 vs retrained CNN+LSTM 0.336, 2D CNN 0.366, FCN 0.400; mean R2 0.683 vs 0.661, 0.633, 0.598; one speaker, single runs
limitations: One Hungarian speaker reading aloud; MSE and R2 of vocoder parameters only, no F0, no listening, intelligibility or ASR test; no seeds or variance; context width not matched across models; CNN+LSTM retrained with changed sizes; no silent articulation or latency.

title: A comparison of oscillatory characteristics in covert speech and speech perception
authors: Jae Moon; Silvia Orlandi; Tom Chau
summary: EEG analysis comparing oscillatory activity in covert speech and speech perception in eight participants; finds stronger low-gamma for covert speech, stronger delta/theta for perception, and theta-gamma coupling.
sensor: EEG cap
vocabulary: Small fixed lexicon of 1-2 syllable words
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Eight-participant study with a small lexicon; no SSI decoder, user study or deployment, and visible participant variability.

title: An Overview of Deep-Learning-Based Audio-Visual Speech Enhancement and Separation
authors: Daniel Michelsanti; Zheng-Hua Tan; Shi-Xiong Zhang; Yong Xu; Meng Yu; Dong Yu; Jesper Jensen
summary: Survey of deep-learning audio-visual speech enhancement and separation, mapping design choices and noting the lack of standardized audio-visual evaluation.
sensor: Microphone and camera (review)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Not a primary SSI contribution; no new benchmark or unified re-evaluation, and lack of standardized evaluation limits performance comparisons.

title: Brain2Char: a deep architecture for decoding text from brain recordings
authors: Pengfei Sun; Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Edward F. Chang
summary: Character CTC decoding from ECoG; all changes are standard. The 7.0-10.6% WER relies on repeated sentences, as the authors concede, and unseen sentences average 80% WER.
sensor: Implanted ECoG grids (16x16, 16x8) on speech cortex
task: Sentence-level text decoding from brain signals
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 7.0-10.6% for three participants on repeated sentences (1200-1900 word vocabularies); unseen sentences average 80% WER
limitations: Invasive implant, per-subject calibration, four participants, best results rely on repeated sentences, no cross-subject transfer.

title: Continuous Silent Speech Recognition using EEG
authors: Gautam Krishna; Co Tran; Mason Carnahan; Ahmed H Tewfik
summary: Standard on silent reading (M04) and CTC decoding (M06); 83% WER on 30 sentences repeated in training, with an undisclosed 4-gram LM and no chance baseline, does not show EEG decoding.
sensor: 31-channel wet scalp EEG (32-electrode cap incl. ground, 10-20 placement), 1000 Hz; five statistical features per channel at 100 Hz, KPCA to 20 dimensions
task: Continuous character-level CTC recognition of silently read sentences from EEG, with beam search and an external 4-gram language model
vocabulary: First 30 USC-TIMIT sentences; test subsets of 5 to 30 unique sentences, all repeated in training
speaker: Four male participants (three non-native English speakers); one train-on-three, test-on-fourth run
session: Three repetitions of the 30 sentences per participant; session boundaries not stated
key_result: 83.34% WER on 72 test recordings covering all 30 sentences (74.86% to 84.08% across subsets); 92.55% WER on a held-out subject.
limitations: Test sentences repeat training sentences; language-model corpus and weight not reported; no chance or shuffled-label baseline; single runs without seeds; sentence displayed on screen, so reading and inner speech are not separated.

title: Digital Voicing of Silent Speech
venue: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
authors: David Gaddy; Dan Klein
summary: Silent-EMG target transfer (M02) extends a 2016 DTW recipe; the open corpus scored by WER (M12) became the shared test bed. Headline 94% gain is closed-vocabulary, 20 clips, one evaluator.
sensor: Facial and throat surface EMG electrodes
vocabulary: Closed dates/times set; open vocabulary of 9828 words
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 3.6% human WER closed vocabulary; 74.8% human WER open vocabulary
limitations: Speaker-dependent with substantial data collection; open-vocabulary WER remains high and all results come from the authors' own data setup.

title: Silent Speech Interfaces for Speech Restoration: A Review
authors: Jose A. Gonzalez-Lopez; Alejandro Gomez-Alanis; Juan M. Martin-Donas; Jose L. Perez-Cordoba; Angel M. Gomez
summary: Review of SSI modalities for speech restoration, focusing on deployment bottlenecks such as latency, scarce patient data and modality trade-offs; cites ideal latency of about 50 ms, acceptable up to 100 ms.
sensor: Multimodal biosignal and articulator sensors (review)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: A review that synthesizes uneven prior results without a unified benchmark and does not itself resolve deployment obstacles.

title: Speech Prediction in Silent Videos using Variational Autoencoders
authors: Ravindra Yadav; Ashish Sardana; Vinay P Namboodiri; Rajesh M Hegde
summary: Variational autoencoder model for speech synthesis from silent lip video that models one-to-many ambiguity; on GRID reports STOI 0.724, ESTOI 0.540 and PESQ 1.932, leading Lip2Wav on ESTOI and PESQ.
sensor: Camera (silent lip video)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: STOI 0.724, ESTOI 0.540, PESQ 1.932 on GRID
limitations: Limited to the GRID benchmark with Griffin-Lim waveform recovery; no speaker-independent, open-world or real-time evaluation.

title: Ultra2Speech -- A Deep Learning Framework for Formant Frequency Estimation and Tracking from Ultrasound Tongue Images
authors: Pramit Saha; Yadong Liu; Bryan Gick; Sidney Fels
summary: Estimates and tracks formant frequencies from ultrasound tongue image sequences for speech synthesis; best U2F configuration reaches mean R2 99.96 on joint f1-f2 prediction versus 90.01 for a Conv-BiLSTM baseline.
sensor: Ultrasound probe (tongue images)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Mean R2 99.96 on joint f1-f2 prediction vs 90.01 baseline
limitations: Focuses on formant tracking and vowel trajectories rather than full speech reconstruction; single collected dataset, no cross-speaker or real-time device evaluation.

title: Vocoder-Based Speech Synthesis from Silent Videos
authors: Daniel Michelsanti; Olga Slizovskaia; Gloria Haro; Emilia Gómez; Zheng-Hua Tan; Jesper Jensen
summary: WORLD features (M06) beat the 2019 GAN on seen GRID speakers; on unseen ones PESQ ties and ESTOI is higher. The CTC text loss (M02) adds under 0.015 ESTOI; the WER is the text head's.
sensor: Camera (silent frontal face/mouth video)
speaker: Both
key_result: Seen GRID speakers: PESQ 1.90, ESTOI 0.455 against 0.329 for the 2019 GAN; unseen speakers: ESTOI 0.227 against 0.198 with PESQ tied (1.23 against 1.24). WER 15.1% (seen) and 51.6% (unseen) is from the CTC text head, not ASR on the speech.
limitations: GRID only, one run per configuration with the checkpoint chosen by PESQ; text loss adds under 0.015 ESTOI; no ASR on the synthesized speech, no chance level, and the real-time claim has no latency figure.

title: A Novel Task-Oriented Text Corpus in Silent Speech Recognition and its Natural Language Generation Construction Method
authors: Dong Cao; Dongdong Zhang; HaiBo Chen
summary: Proposes a task-oriented text corpus and a hybrid natural language generation method for building EEG silent speech recognition datasets; claims gains over template and neural NLG but gives no numeric benchmark.
sensor: EEG headset
task: Corpus construction for EEG silent speech recognition
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Does not solve EEG decoding, relies on a narrow domain, and quantitative evidence is too weak to audit the comparative claims.

title: Autoencoder-Based Articulatory-to-Acoustic Mapping for Ultrasound Silent Speech Interfaces
authors: Gábor Gosztolya; Ádám Pintér; László Tóth; Tamás Grósz; Alexandra Markó; Tamás Gábor Csapó
summary: Standard on the encoder: autoencoder features predate it and it is never compared with PCA or DCT; behind on F0, which is copied from the recording, so the listening test is not of a silent system.
sensor: Midsagittal ultrasound tongue imaging, Articulate Instruments Micro, 82 fps, resized to 64x128
task: Ultrasound-to-spectrum estimation (25 MGC-LSP plus gain) for direct synthesis, with autoencoder bottleneck features as input
vocabulary: Read Hungarian sentences (vocalized); vocabulary not stated
speaker: One female speaker; train, development and test from the same speaker
session: Not stated; session-disjoint splits not reported
key_result: Test NMSE 0.534 (pixels, 1 frame) to 0.377 (autoencoder N=256, 13 frames); MUSHRA naturalness 16.58 to 40.98 against 75.16 for vocoded speech, with original F0.
limitations: Only a raw-pixel baseline, no PCA or DCT; F0 copied from the recording; configuration named on development and test scores together; one speaker; no seeds, significance test or intelligibility test.

title: Denoising convolutional autoencoder based B-mode ultrasound tongue image feature extraction
authors: Bo Li; Kele Xu; Dawei Feng; Haibo Mi; Huaimin Wang; Jian Zhu
summary: Uses a denoising convolutional autoencoder to extract ultrasound tongue image features, improving silent speech recognition over prior feature extraction methods on the 2010 Silent Speech Challenge data.
sensor: Ultrasound tongue imaging (4-8 MHz microconvex probe)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: WER 6.17% with DCAE features, single-speaker Silent Speech Challenge data
limitations: Single-speaker dataset only, no cross-corpus validation, and robustness to different ultrasound systems and head movement is not validated.

title: Lipper: Synthesizing Thy Speech using Multi-View Lipreading
authors: Yaman Kumar; Rohit Jain; Khwaja Mohd. Salik; Rajiv Ratn Shah; Yifang Yin; Roger Zimmermann
summary: Lipper reconstructs speech from multi-view lip video on OuluVS2 as a regression problem; the best three-view setting reaches PESQ 2.315 with 0.169 s end-to-end delay, though audio remains robotic.
sensor: Multi-view cameras (lip video)
task: Speech synthesis from multi-view lip video
vocabulary: OuluVS2 phrases, including OOV phrase tests
speaker: Both
key_result: PESQ 2.315 (0 deg+45 deg+60 deg views), 0.169 s delay; user study 80.25% audio-only accuracy
limitations: Robotic audio, lips alone cannot recover prosody, controlled OuluVS2 conditions only, and weak speaker-independent results.

title: SottoVoce: An Ultrasound Imaging-Based Silent Speech Interaction Using Deep Neural Networks
authors: Naoki Kimura; Michinari Kono; Jun Rekimoto
summary: SottoVoce reconstructs speech audio from under-jaw ultrasound images with two DNNs to control unmodified smart speakers; command success rose from 42.5% to 65.0% with the second network, versus 90.0% for real audio.
sensor: 3.5 MHz convex ultrasound probe under the jaw
task: Speech synthesis from ultrasound for voice-assistant control
vocabulary: ~500 training commands; 4 Alexa commands in end-to-end test
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 65.0% smart speaker command success (4 commands x5, two networks) vs 90.0% ground-truth audio
limitations: Only two participants, speaker-dependent, tiny end-to-end command set, bulky non-wearable probe, 2.61 s latency, and unassessed ultrasound safety.

title: Speech synthesis from neural decoding of spoken sentences
authors: Gopala K. Anumanchipalli; Josh Chartier; Edward F. Chang
summary: Two-stage bLSTM decoder maps ECoG during reading aloud to inferred articulatory features and then to acoustic parameters, synthesizing sentence waveforms (median MCD 5.14-6.58 dB in five participants). The two-stage model beat a direct decoder by 0.54 dB in P1, but the intermediate targets add phonetic-label supervision and the decoders differ in depth and learning rate; listener transcription used closed 25/50-word pools.
sensor: Clinical high-density ECoG (high gamma 70-200 Hz and 1-30 Hz)
task: Sentence-level speech synthesis from neural signals
vocabulary: Read sentences (MOCHA-TIMIT and others); closed 25/50-word pools for listener transcription
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: Median MCD 5.14-6.58 dB; 0.54 dB better than direct decoding (P1); listener median WER 31% (25-word pool) and 53% (50-word pool)
limitations: Decoder comparison and listener tests in P1 only, repetitions not stated; extra phonetic supervision in the intermediate stage (the authors tried a 6-layer direct decoder and kept the better 4-layer one); closed-pool transcription without chance level; mimed-speech values (58 trials of 10 sentences) in figures only, with inconsistent counts; read from the author manuscript (bioRxiv 2018-11 and published versions not compared).

title: Ultrasound-based Silent Speech Interface Built on a Continuous Vocoder
authors: Tamás Gábor Csapó; Mohammed Salah Al-Radhi; Géza Németh; Gábor Gosztolya; Tamás Grósz; László Tóth; Alexandra Markó
summary: Continuous F0 targets from articulation were prior work; MVF carrying voicing instead of a flag is new but unproven: the F0 RMSE gain uses different reference contours and naturalness is not better.
sensor: Midsagittal ultrasound tongue imaging (Micro system, 81.67 fps), one 64x128 frame per prediction
task: Ultrasound-to-speech synthesis with a continuous vocoder (continuous F0, maximum voiced frequency, MGC-LSP)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: ContF0 RMSE 30.56 Hz vs 65.34 Hz for discontinuous F0, measured against different reference contours; MUSHRA naturalness 43.45 vs 40.87 with predicted excitation and original spectra, not significant; four speakers, 9 test sentences each
limitations: Continuous F0 targets from articulation were prior work; RMSE comparison not like-for-like and untested; no significant naturalness gain; no intelligibility test, no flag-plus-continuous-F0 control, no seeds; speaker-dependent, vocalized speech only; real-time claim unmeasured.

title: Video-Driven Speech Reconstruction using Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Konstantinos Vougioukas; Pingchuan Ma; Stavros Petridis; Maja Pantic
summary: Direct-waveform GAN (M06) and speech-encoder perceptual loss (M02) are early but standard; the perceptual loss carries the words. Unseen-speaker WER 40.5% (successor 16%); no listener test.
sensor: Camera (silent frontal face video)
speaker: Both
key_result: Seen GRID speakers: ASR WER 26.6%, STOI 0.518 (Lip2AudSpec 32.5%, 0.446), PESQ 1.71 below Lip2AudSpec 1.82; without the perceptual loss WER 83.3%. Unseen speakers: WER 40.5%, STOI 0.445, PESQ 1.24.
limitations: GRID only, single runs, no listener test or chance level; a persistent hum lowers PESQ; unseen speakers get wrong-gender or morphing voices and 40% to 60% WER per speaker; the perceptual encoder's training speakers are unstated; frontal faces only.

title: AlterEgo: A Personalized Wearable Silent Speech Interface
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI '18), pp. 43-53
authors: Arnav Kapur; Shreyas Kapur; Pattie Maes
summary: Wearable headset that recognizes silently articulated words from face and jaw neuromuscular signals and answers through bone-conduction audio; abstract reports 92% median word accuracy in user studies.
sensor: Head-worn surface EMG electrodes on face and jaw, with bone-conduction headphones
vocabulary: Small task vocabularies (about 20 words per application, per MIT News)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 92% median word accuracy in user studies (abstract)
limitations: Small closed vocabularies and per-user customization; full protocol (splits, sessions, architecture) not verified because only the abstract and press coverage were available.

title: Deep Audio-Visual Speech Recognition
authors: Triantafyllos Afouras; Joon Son Chung; Andrew Senior; Oriol Vinyals; Andrew Zisserman
summary: Landmark AVSR paper that releases LRS2-BBC and compares CTC and sequence-to-sequence Transformers on one shared encoder. Video-only TM-seq2seq reaches 48.3% WER with an LM (49.8% without; the 70.4% WAS baseline has no stated decoding conditions, and the same group's Transformer three months earlier already reached 50.0%). CTC and seq2seq differ little once an LM or audio is added.
sensor: Face/mouth video (25 fps, 112 px mouth crop) plus 16 kHz audio
task: Sentence-level lip reading and audio-visual speech recognition
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 48.3% WER video-only (LRS2-BBC, +LM); 8.2% audio-visual clean; 23.6% audio-visual in 0 dB babble
limitations: Test speakers may overlap with training (split by broadcast date, speaker count unreported); single runs; matched synthetic babble noise only; pretraining uses non-public MV-LRS; GPU model inconsistent between sections.

title: Development of sEMG sensors and algorithms for silent speech recognition
authors: Geoffrey S. Meltzner; James T. Heaton; Yunbin Deng; Gianluca De Luca; Serge H. Roy; Joshua C. Kline
summary: Face- and neck-worn sEMG sensors with staged recognition algorithms decode silently mouthed phrases; abstract reports 8.9% WER on 1,200+ phrases from a 2,200-word vocabulary.
sensor: Face- and neck-worn surface EMG sensors
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 8.9% WER (91.1% recognition rate), 2,200-word vocabulary
limitations: Reviewed from the abstract only; participants, speaker dependence, grammar constraints and session design were not verified.

title: Harnessing AI for Speech Reconstruction using Multi-view Silent Video Feed
venue: Proceedings of the 26th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM '18)
authors: Yaman Kumar; Mayank Aggarwal; Pratham Nawal; Shin'ichi Satoh; Rajiv Ratn Shah; Roger Zimmermann
summary: Multi-view input (M05) is new for video-to-speech but standard on its evidence: 2 speakers, gains overstated (11.4% in Table 1, 26% in text); PESQ only, no listener test (M12).
sensor: Two of five synchronized OuluVS2 camera views (0/30/45/60/90 deg)
task: Speech waveform reconstruction from multi-view silent video
vocabulary: OuluVS2 phrases, digit sequences and TIMIT sentences
speaker: Two reported speakers (1 and 10); training split not stated
key_result: PESQ 1.9683 / 1.9978 for 0+30 deg against 1.7674 / 1.7812 for 0 deg (Table 1)
limitations: Two speakers, no repeats or split stated, best pairs only, PESQ only with no listener test; every stated gain exceeds Table 1.

title: Lip2AudSpec: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Lip Movements Video
venue: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Hassan Akbari; Himani Arora; Liangliang Cao; Nima Mesgarani
summary: Bottleneck target (M02) and auditory-spectrogram route (M06) are standard; gains rest on one speaker, a re-implemented baseline and a vocabulary-cued test on four seen GRID speakers.
sensor: Camera (silent lip video)
task: Speech synthesis from silent lip video
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Human word accuracy 55.8% vs 50.9% baseline; STMI 0.80 vs 0.52, four GRID speakers
limitations: Only four GRID speakers and closed vocabulary; lip-only input misses tongue and throat cues; no real-world recordings.

title: Updating the Silent Speech Challenge benchmark with deep learning
authors: Yan Ji; Licheng Liu; Hongcui Wang; Zhilei Liu; Zhibin Niu; Bruce Denby
summary: Kaldi DNN-HMM cuts SSC WER from 17.4% to 6.45% (M06, M12: standard), but with the same bigram its own GMM gives 12.71%, so the DNN halves WER; one speaker, single runs.
sensor: Under-chin ultrasound transducer plus lip camera
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 6.45% WER on the SSC test (Kaldi DNN-HMM, 30 DCT features, closed WSJ 5k bigram) vs the 17.4% benchmark; with the same bigram the paper's own triphone2b GMM-HMM gives 12.71%, and the less task-specific CSR 5k bigram gives 11.44%.
limitations: One speaker, 1023 test words, single runs without seeds or significance tests; only 5k-vocabulary WSJ0 bigram language models; the DAE advantage at 5 dimensions rests on DCT runs that fail (98-100% WER), a collapse the paper leaves unexplained.

title: Visual-Only Recognition of Normal, Whispered and Silent Speech
venue: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: Stavros Petridis; Jie Shen; Doruk Cetin; Maja Pantic
summary: Ahead on data: the first public three-mode lip-video corpus. Standard on transfer: the silent drop was known, and most of it is test-mode difficulty, not the training mode.
sensor: Video cameras, frontal view used (45-degree and profile recorded)
task: Closed-set visual-only utterance classification across normal, whispered and silent speech
speaker: Speaker-independent (digits 30/10/13, phrases 20/8/11 train/validation/test speakers)
key_result: Normal-trained: 68.0 to 59.7% (digits) and 69.7 to 61.2% (phrases) from normal to silent test; on the silent test, silent training gains only 2.5 and 3.2 points over normal training, and whispered training is best for silent phrases (65.1%).
limitations: Closed 10-class tasks; train-mode and test-mode effects not separated; no significance tests or chance level; seeds and stopping rule not stated; utterance boundaries still under correction at publication.

title: Biosignal-Based Spoken Communication: A Survey
venue: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing 25(12), 2257-2271
authors: Tanja Schultz; Michael Wand; Thomas Hueber; Dean J. Krusienski; Christian Herff; Jonathan S. Brumberg
summary: Survey that frames silent speech within biosignal-based spoken communication, spanning articulatory, muscular and neural signals for communication devices, rehabilitation and speech science.
sensor: Articulatory, muscular and neural biosignal sensors (review)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Reviewed from the abstract only; a survey without a unified benchmark, so its detailed comparisons were not checked.

title: Improved Speech Reconstruction from Silent Video
venue: 2017 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops (ICCVW)
authors: Ariel Ephrat; Tavi Halperin; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Optical-flow tower (M05) and mel-to-linear post-net (M06) are standard: no flow gain in Table 5; trails Le Cornu on S3; no listener test (M12); Lip2Wav's re-run: 27.83% vs 14.08% WER.
sensor: Camera (full-face video plus optical flow)
vocabulary: 51-word GRID grammar plus unseen words in TCD-TIMIT
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: GRID S4 STOI 0.700 vs 0.584 for Vid2speech, but behind Le Cornu and Milner on S3 ESTOI (0.398 vs 0.437) and PESQ; in Lip2Wav's re-run of the method, 27.83% GRID WER vs 14.08% for Lip2Wav
limitations: Speaker-dependent; objective metrics only, no listener or ASR test; single splits without seeds or intervals; optical-flow tower shows no gain in its ablation; post-net gain comes from a row mixing two synthesis paths; TCD-TIMIT result holds for one of three speakers.

title: Lip Reading Sentences in the Wild
authors: Joon Son Chung; Andrew Senior; Oriol Vinyals; Andrew Zisserman
summary: Introduces Watch, Listen, Attend and Spell and the BBC LRS dataset. Lips-only decoding reaches 50.2% WER on open-vocabulary broadcast sentences against 73.8% for a professional lipreader, but the lipreader worked on 200 clips under different viewing conditions with declined clips excluded (87.6% with them), and the machine score is not stated to be on the same clips. The word-to-sentence curriculum gives the largest single gain (76.5% to 61.1%), from one training run.
sensor: Camera (broadcast mouth crops, 120 px grey, 25 Hz), optional audio (13-dim MFCC)
task: Sentence-level lip reading and audio-visual speech recognition
speaker: Not stated
key_result: 50.2% lips-only WER on LRS (professional lipreader 73.8% on 200 clips); 13.9% audio-visual WER clean vs 17.7% audio-only; 3.0% WER on GRID (overlapped-speaker split)
limitations: Train/test speaker overlap unreported (date split only); single runs; human comparison under unequal conditions; noise type at test unstated; LRS was never released.

title: Seeing Through Noise: Visually Driven Speaker Separation and Enhancement
authors: Aviv Gabbay; Ariel Ephrat; Tavi Halperin; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Uses visual speech predictions from face video to build masks that separate or enhance a target speaker from audio mixtures, beating audio-only separation on GRID and TCD-TIMIT. Not an SSI paper.
sensor: Camera plus microphone (face video and audio)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: GRID separation SDR 5.62, PESQ 2.6 vs audio-only 1.74, 1.85
limitations: Not SSI; speaker-dependent models, unknown speakers need fine-tuning, and evaluation uses synthetic two-speaker mixtures.

title: Vid2speech: Speech Reconstruction from Silent Video
authors: Ariel Ephrat; Shmuel Peleg
summary: Vid2speech reconstructs intelligible speech from silent face video on GRID with speaker-specific models and LPC-style resynthesis, reaching about 80% human intelligibility and partial out-of-vocabulary recovery.
sensor: Camera (GRID face video, 25 fps)
speaker: Speaker-dependent
key_result: 82.6% audio-only intelligibility (S4) vs 40.0% prior work; OOV 51.6% vs 10% chance
limitations: Speaker-specific training, constrained GRID grammar, unnatural-sounding resynthesis, and a small listening study without open-vocabulary or live testing.

title: Contour-based 3d tongue motion visualization using ultrasound image sequences
authors: Kele Xu; Yin Yang; Clemence Leboullenger; Pierre Roussel; Bruce Denby
summary: Builds a contour-based pipeline that maps midsagittal ultrasound tongue contours to 3D tongue motion using a database of 1000 3D shapes; evaluation is qualitative, with about 1.2 s per frame association.
sensor: B-mode ultrasound tongue imaging
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported (about 1.2 s average to associate a frame with the 3D model)
limitations: Not a recognizer; uses only midsagittal information with a simplified driving scheme and has no quantitative accuracy benchmark.

title: LipNet: End-to-End Sentence-level Lipreading
authors: Yannis M. Assael; Brendan Shillingford; Shimon Whiteson; Nando de Freitas
summary: End-to-end lipreader (spatiotemporal CNN, Bi-GRU, CTC) decoding GRID sentences from video; 4.8% WER on overlapped speakers and 11.4% on unseen speakers.
sensor: Camera (frontal face/lip video)
speaker: Both
key_result: 4.8% WER overlapped speakers, 11.4% WER unseen speakers on GRID
limitations: Only GRID's tiny fixed grammar with vocalized speech; no open vocabulary, in-the-wild, silent-articulation or real-time evaluation.

title: Silent speech interfaces
authors: Bruce Denby; Tanja Schultz; Kiyoshi Honda; Thomas Hueber; James M. Gilbert; Jonathan S. Brumberg
summary: Founding review that defines silent speech interfaces, surveys seven sensing technologies from EMA to intracortical implants, and scores them on six practical criteria; concludes no technology meets all of them.
sensor: Seven SSI technology families (review)
speaker: Not stated
key_result: Not reported
limitations: Pre-deep-learning review; cited results are small-vocabulary and heterogeneous, and the comparison scores are qualitative.
